summary: Tested new EMAIL BACKUPS feature end-to-end. Backend: new pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_email_backups.py — 14/14 PASSED covering GET/PUT /api/settings/email (password masked, has_password bool, raw password never returned), PUT persistence, password retention when the field is omitted or sent as empty string, POST /api/email/test (400 when host/to missing, 502 with 'Could not send email: ...' when SMTP host unreachable — verified against localhost:8001 to bypass CF edge), POST /api/backups/{name}/email returns 404 for a non-existent file, and Viewer gets 403 on GET/PUT /settings/email, POST /email/test and POST /backups/{name}/email. Regression smoke on /settings/backup, /backups and /data/export still OK. Frontend: Settings → Backup & Restore renders the Email Backups card with every spec'd testid; saved config persists after reload (smtp.example.com, 587, t@example.com, from=t@example.com, to=treasurer@church.org, enabled on); password field is empty on reload and the hint '(saved — leave blank to keep)' is shown (confirms masking); Save with blank password keeps has_password=true (hint still visible after save); Viewer login on /settings shows NO Backup tab. CRITICAL UX FINDING: Send Test Email surfaces the WRONG error message because the preview ingress (Cloudflare) intercepts the backend's 502 and replaces the JSON body with its own 'The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare…' detail, which the toast then displays verbatim. The backend itself returns the correct '{"detail": "Could not send email: [Errno -2] Name or service not known"}' on localhost — only the public URL is affected.

minor.issue: Returning HTTP 502 for application-level SMTP failures causes the Cloudflare ingress to replace the response body with a generic Cloudflare 502 HTML/JSON, hiding the real 'Could not send email: ...' detail from the frontend toast. Consider using a 4xx status (e.g. 400 or 422) or 503 with a structured JSON error — Cloudflare only rewrites 5xx from origin.

integration_issues.flow: Settings → Backup & Restore → Email Backups → Send Test Email
integration_issues.issue: Error toast shows the Cloudflare bad-gateway message ('The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare. This typically indicates the origin is overloaded or misconfigured.') instead of the backend's 'Could not send email: ...' detail. Root cause is the backend returning 502 — the preview ingress rewrites 5xx responses. Fix on the backend (change the status to a 4xx) will make the clear message reach the toast.

action_items: HIGH: Change POST /api/email/test and POST /api/backups/{name}/email to return a 4xx status (e.g. 400 or 422) for SMTP/configuration failures so the detail message reaches the client through the ingress; 5xx responses are rewritten by Cloudflare and hide the real error from the user toast. Alternative: keep 502 but have the frontend show a static 'Could not send email — check SMTP host, credentials, and that the port is reachable.' instead of relying on response.data.detail when status is 5xx.
critical_code_review_comments: EmailConfig uses `smtp_password: Optional[str] = None` and update_email_config retains the existing hash when the field is None or ''. Verified both branches with tests. Good.
GET /settings/email omits smtp_password entirely and exposes has_password:bool — matches spec; no sensitive leakage.
All four email endpoints are gated by require_data (data.manage) — Viewer 403 verified for every one of them.

_send_email_sync handles both STARTTLS (port 587) and SMTP_SSL (port 465). Only concern: no explicit asyncio timeout wrapping of asyncio.to_thread — a hanging SMTP connect could hold a worker thread for up to 30s (socket timeout is set, so it's bounded).
Status-code choice for SMTP failures (502) is a documented bug in this preview environment — Cloudflare rewrites 5xx bodies. See action_items. This is the only user-visible defect found.

maybe_email_backup() swallows exceptions and only logs — fine for the scheduled job (don't break the nightly), but consider also persisting the last-error to settings so the UI can surface 'Last email failed at ...' later.
Settings.js EmailBackupCard is ~65 lines and self-contained — fine. formatApiErrorDetail is reused for both save and test, so if detail is a Pydantic validation list it will still render reasonably.

success_rate.frontend: 95% — all UI/persistence/masking/permission flows pass; Send Test Email surfaces a wrong (Cloudflare-rewritten) message due to the 502 status code choice

Backend endpoints: GET/PUT /api/settings/email, POST /api/email/test, POST /api/backups/{name}/email — all gated by data.manage. Preview ingress rewrites 5xx bodies: when verifying the 'Could not send email: ...' string via backend_test, hit http://localhost:8001 directly (public URL will show the Cloudflare 502 detail). Pytest invocation: `pytest backend/tests/test_email_backups.py -v -o addopts=''`.
rca of the issue: Send Test Email shows a Cloudflare-flavoured error toast. RCA: backend raises HTTPException(status_code=502, detail='Could not send email: ...') on SMTP failures. In this preview environment the public URL goes through the Cloudflare edge, which treats any 5xx from origin as a bad-gateway condition and REPLACES the response body with its own JSON ({ title:'Error 502: Bad gateway', detail:'The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare...' }). The frontend's toast.error(formatApiErrorDetail(e.response.data.detail)) therefore shows the Cloudflare message, not the real one. Reproduction: in Settings → Backup → Email Backups, with the saved smtp.example.com config, click Send Test Email → wait ~2s → toast reads 'The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare...'. Verified on localhost that FastAPI returns the correct body; only the ingress-fronted path is affected. Mitigation (backend, preferred): change POST /email/test and POST /backups/{name}/email to raise 400/422 for SMTP/config failures — 4xx bodies pass through Cloudflare untouched. Alternative (frontend): when response.status is in [502,503,504], ignore response.data.detail and show a hard-coded 'Could not send email — check SMTP host, port and credentials.' Either fix will satisfy the 'clear error toast' requirement.
